To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) correctness is an important issue for multi-server game architectures, (ii) correctness mechanisms can be implemented to reduce the amount of incorrectly processed user inputs and (iii) correctness mechanisms can also be optimized to reduce the amount and frequency of the required correctness checks.
we have shown the correctness problem for multi-server replication and have presented a solution for the correctness problem in the form of a lag mechanism.

we have developed and implemented a correctness mechanism that is able to reduce the number of incorrectly ordered actions from 50% down to 10% and that we have shown that the timewarp mechanism is not suitable for multi-server replication.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the correctness of multi-server replication architectures in massively multiplayer games and the development of mechanisms to preserve the order in which user input is processed.
the development of correctness mechanisms for scalable, parallel multi-server game architectures.
the correctness of massively multiplayer online games and provides an analysis of the problem and a first solution for correctness in multi-server replication architectures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

lag is an effective mechanism to ensure correctness of replicated game state, but that it has to be applied in combination with other mechanisms to provide a high performance and scalable replication architecture.
the lag mechanism is the most promising approach for correctness in multi-server replication architectures.
correctness mechanisms for multi-server replication in online games are necessary and can be efficiently implemented.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide the first correctness mechanism for multi-server replication in online games.
the correctness issue in multi-server replication architectures has been identified and that the lag mechanism is a promising approach to preserve the order in the virtual processing.
the lag-based mechanism can be used as a simple, efficient, and scalable solution for correctness of multi-server state replication architectures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
correctness of game state processing is an important issue in massively multiplayer online games and should be considered when developing and implementing multi-server game architectures.
correctness is a crucial factor for the quality of massively multiplayer online games.
the correctness of the game world state is a crucial issue for multi-server game architectures.
